findings.finding: Legacy environment, arbitrary frame, prebuffered socket, fork/descriptor transfer, replay, and held-open input cannot select child success and refuse with zero writes.
Production spawn requires RootBrokerAuthorization; its private Infallible field has no source-local production constructor or serialization path, and the live gate always refuses.

The process-path probe enters the real bounded executor with immutable /usr/bin/true and real root/read/output descriptors, observes broker-required before Started, and records zero spawn and unchanged state.

Same-UID N06 state cannot authenticate a same-executable parent. A different-principal root broker must own durable reservation and signing state, directly answer a post-exec child challenge, atomically bind request/protocol/intent/node/program object/PID/session/frame digest, and consume one use before stdin.
Four broker-backed immutable-runtime public journeys remain ignored; no installed/public success or legitimate internal-child positive claim is made.
Recovery/reuse is 36/2; the last broad routine_work run before the final proof-only delta was 69/27 under the managed-temp secret-path conflict plus one provenance compiler collision.
Strict library compilation is red at 649 diagnostics with 31 routine-path mentions.

Replace require_root_broker_before_spawn with a root-owned different-principal broker adapter. It must own non-exportable signing/reservation state, validate the exact durable Reserved record, answer a fresh post-exec challenge directly, bind exact request/protocol/intent/node/program object/parent-child PID/session/frame digest, CAS Reserved to Started once, and only then permit stdin; no file-only same-UID authority is sufficient.

Provision an exact immutable installed Ultragoal runtime and execute the four broker-backed journeys plus positive internal child, cancellation, descendant reaping, setup-failure, sandbox, and replay controls.
Reconcile required .codex-worktree isolated temp roots with the legacy secret-path prohibition without weakening either boundary.
